What's new in Vekrun 0.6.9: Capabilities — the tools, connections and skills Vekrun can use

• One list: Capabilities shows your command-line tools, MCP connections and skills together, in one set of words (Ready, Installed, Needs sign-in, Needs review, …). Installed never reads as Ready, and each one's details say where it can run, where it came from, and every check behind its status. Open it from Connections ("All capabilities"), Settings → Skills, or the command palette.
• Import skills from GitHub or a folder: paste a link such as github.com/mattpocock/skills, see every skill it holds at an exact commit (scripts named, anything Vekrun doesn't use said plainly), and install only the ones you pick, for you or for this project. Installing never trusts a skill; trust it from its details, at its exact files. Later, "Check for updates" shows the lines that change in each file (scripts first) and lets you keep the current version, update, or keep both; if you edited your copy, it says so and offers to keep it or restore the source's. Trust never carries over to new files.
• Import MCP servers from Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf or Codex, or from a GitHub repository's MCP manifest. You see each server's exact command or URL before adding it; its API keys go straight to the keychain and never appear on screen; its tools still ask until you review them.
• Skill Studio: write a skill yourself, or describe it and let the coding agent you already connected draft it. It's checked as you type: a skill can't grant itself permissions or tell an agent to skip verification, approve its own work or change delivery.
• As you type a goal, the Factory says which connections and tools it will use, what needs a step first ("Linear: review its tools", which opens Linear), and services it names that aren't set up yet. If you start anyway, Factory asks first: set them up, or start without them — and then the run is told, so the parts that needed them are reported as not done, never as finished.
• Save approach as skill: from a verified or delivered Work Item, turn how it was done into a reusable skill.
• Register a command-line tool already on this Mac (stripe, terraform…): Vekrun finds it, notes its version, notices if its file changes, and says whether a Work Item's VM can have it. Nothing is installed.
• Capabilities used: a Work Item shows what its runs actually used — the skills given to the agent (at their exact files) and the MCP tools it called — apart from what was only available to them (tools offered but never called, tools on this Mac).
• Skills can be removed (recoverably), and connections and tools lead you to where they're managed.
• From the command line you can only tighten: withdraw a skill's trust, deny an MCP tool, narrow what runs without asking. Trusting a skill, reviewing a connection's tools, letting calls run without asking and taking a server out of confinement are decisions you make in the app.
• An MCP import you preview but don't add no longer keeps its values on disk.
• Fixes: an updated skill's kept-aside previous version no longer shows up as a second live skill; a skill at the root of a repository is named after itself; a signed-in GitHub CLI reads Ready.
